title: What is bullying, and what is not?
examples: Is an argument the same as bullying?
How do I know if I am being bullied?

explain.say: Here is a question: if a friend is grumpy with you once, is that bullying? Not quite! Look at the two groups on the board, and let us sort it out together.

draw.text: What is bullying, and what is not?

explain.say: See the bullying group? Bullying is being mean on purpose, again and again, in a way that is hard for you to stop. Shutting someone out on purpose, and mean posts online, count too.
Now look at the other group: a one-off argument, an accident or falling out once. These can still hurt, but they are not bullying. Can you think of the difference?
Here is a quick check. Was it on purpose? Does it keep happening? Is it hard to make it stop? If the answer is yes to these, it is bullying. Look at the ticks on the board.

faq.a: Bullying is hurting someone on purpose, again and again, when it is hard for them to stop it. It can be hitting, name-calling, leaving out, spreading rumours or being mean online.

faq.q: Is an argument the same as bullying?
faq.a: No. An argument between friends who both have a say is a disagreement. It becomes bullying when one person keeps hurting the other on purpose.
asks: Tell me about the Not bullying

faq.q: What does power mean in bullying?
faq.a: It means the person being bullied finds it hard to stop it, maybe because the bully is older, bigger, more popular or has a group with them.

faq.q: Who should I tell about bullying?
faq.a: A parent or carer, a teacher, a school counsellor or another trusted adult. If one adult does not help, tell another.

faq.q: Is it my fault if I am bullied?
faq.a: Never. Bullying is a choice the bully makes. Nobody deserves to be bullied, whatever they look like or whoever they are.

facts: A 2019 UNESCO report found that almost one in three students worldwide had been bullied at least once in the past month.
Bullying is usually defined as unwanted, aggressive behaviour that is repeated and involves a real or perceived imbalance of power.
